dod_intent_evidence: Own site sells anti-jam/EW products to 'military operators' with native ATAK integration; AF STTR PhII 2022 ($750k) and AF SBIR PhI 2024 in their own abstracts and SBIR records.
score_evidence: Spec-brag framing on product pages: 'Real-time jammer geolocation (±50m CEP)', 'one-degree organic direction finding', 'Mass producible' comparison tables → lab_language_intensity

Fluent deployment vocabulary keeps awareness subscores low: 'ultra–low-size, weight, and power (SWaP)', 'Modular Open System Architecture (MOSA)-compliant', 'Ruggedized for dismounted & vehicle operations', native ATAK/WinTAK → deployment_awareness_absence, operator_absence

All four open roles are lab-side builds — 'Radio Frequency Engineer', 'Senior Firmware Engineer' (x2 each) — zero field/test/integration or compliance roles while three products are marketed as 'ready to integrate' → hiring_profile_skew
STTR PhII awarded 2022 (period of performance now expired or expiring), a 2024 award back at Phase I ($74,110), ~21 people, no announced fielding or transition of GRALE/VAELIN/TALON → stage_pressure

blind_spots.blind_spot: Products marketed as 'ready to integrate' with no visible transition vehicle — three SBIR/STTR awards since 2021 and no announced fielding, program, or prime teaming
blind_spots.operator_reality: EW modules only reach the field mounted on someone else's platform under someone else's program; without a prime/GFE integration path and an advocate above the operator level, 'ready to integrate' means shelf-ready
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Team is signal-processing PhDs and engineers; the site's fluency is technical, not acquisition — nothing about contracts, primes, or programs anywhere
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Anti-jamming, resilient command-and-control, and protected navigation — ready to integrate.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Sells identical EW/anti-jam modules to commercial logistics and defense with zero ITAR/export language
blind_spots.operator_reality: Jamming detection/cancellation and jammer-geolocation hardware is export-controlled; a dual-market motion without a stated export-control posture stalls both the foreign-partner deals and the DoD paperwork
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Commercial-market ambition ('every port, grid, and pipeline operations center') is written by the same hand as the defense pages, with no compliance layer between them
blind_spots.evidence_quote: The same vulnerabilities that exist on the battlefield exist in every port, grid, and pipeline operations center.

blind_spots.blind_spot: No training or sustainment story for the fielded module — who trains the operator, who swaps it, who supports 'fully autonomous' when it isn't
blind_spots.operator_reality: A 'fully autonomous module' on a drone or handheld still needs the E-5's 20-minute training block, spares, battery/power budget on the platform, and a fix-forward path; none of that appears on any product page
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: TALON's ATAK fluency suggests they know the operator screen but not the sustainment tail behind it
blind_spots.evidence_quote: This ultra–low-size, weight, and power (SWaP), fully autonomous module safeguards communications links

opener_hook: Archaius has three Air Force SBIR/STTR awards since 2021 and markets GRALE, VAELIN, and TALON as ready to integrate — the 2022 STTR PhII period of performance has run out with no announced fielding, which is the exact window where EW startups lose the transition.
what_they_do: Builds anti-jamming, protected-navigation, and ATAK-integrated electronic warfare modules for drones, vehicles, and dismounted operators.
